title: Exact localization component
statement:
theorem grothendieckDerived_exact_localization
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    {S : Type w} [Ring S] [HasDerivedCategory.{max w vH} (ModuleCat.{max w vH} S)]
    (F : ModuleCat.{max w vH} S ⥤ A) (U : A ⥤ ModuleCat.{max w vH} S)
    (adj₀ : F ⊣ U) [F.Additive] [U.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (hc₀ : IsIso adj₀.counit) :
    F.mapDerivedCategory.IsTriangulated ∧
      IsIso adj₀.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction.counit

proof.text: Install the invertible abelian counit as an instance. Adjunction.fullyFaithfulROfIsIsoCounit supplies Full and Faithful for U.

Adjunction.preservesKInjectiveComplexes supplies preservation of K-injective complexes from exactness of F. The proved source library instances Functor.full_rightDerivedFunctor and Functor.faithful_rightDerivedFunctor make the actual U.rightDerivedFunctor fully faithful.

Use the actual adjunction adj₀.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction. Mathlib gives its invertible counit from full faithfulness of the right functor, and gives F.mapDerivedCategory.IsTriangulated directly. Pair these two instances.

proof_origin.place: E2 repair; proved using WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.Adjunction, .Comp and .FullyFaithful, and Mathlib exact-functor and fully-faithful adjunction APIs

statement_change.what: The old Lean signature allows every triangulated source B, including the zero category. An invertible counit would make its right adjoint faithful, forcing the nonzero target derived category to be thin. Replace it with the derived localization of a fixed exact abelian module adjunction with invertible counit; adapt the parent proof without changing its signature.
